items.title: Ben Starr Has One Message for ‘Expedition 33’ Fans: “Let Them Cook” [Exclusive]
items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 star Ben Starr urged fans to be patient for Sandfall Interactive's next project and trust in the studio's creativity.
items.content:
Verso staring outward and speaking in Expedition 33. Image via Sandfall Interactive By Ryan O'Rourke & Maggie Lovitt Published Sep 1, 2026, 7:30 PM EDT Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap 2025 ended as one of the better years for gaming in recent memory , at least for the players. Games that had been in development seemingly forever, like Hollow Knight: Silksong and Metroid Prime 4: Beyond , finally released, while some of the best sequels in recent memory, including Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 , Hades 2 , and Death Stranding: On the Beach , arrived to build upon their already-acclaimed predecessors. Indie titles, too, flourished, as Blue Prince broke players' minds with its puzzles, Dispatch carried on the legacy of classic Telltale games with a mature superhero story, and PEAK became the poster child for the questionably named genre of "Friendslop." Yet, no title is so synonymous with the year as Sandfall Interactive's breakout hit RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

Created by a small team of over 30 developers led by ex-Ubisoft employee Guillaume Broche , Expedition 33 was hailed as a marvel for how it united the JRPG format with a uniquely fantastical French style while telling a story of grief, loss, and creation much deeper than its initial presentation suggests. It follows the titular Expedition 33, the latest group of citizens from the city of Lumière that sets out to destroy The Paintress, a haunting being on the horizon behind a yearly Gommage that erases all people of the ever-decreasing age she paints from existence. After critics and gamers fell in love with the debut title from Sandfall, it went on to win Game of the Year at The Game Awards , along with eight of the 13 other accolades it was nominated for. With the dust now settled on such a singular success, questions are starting to be asked about what comes next for the team with Gustave, Maelle, Verso, Lune, Sciel, and Monoco laid to rest.

On that front, Ben Starr is preaching patience. Over the weekend, the voice of Verso joined his friend and Best Performance Game Award-winner Jennifer English for an Expedition 33 Q&A at Fan Expo Canada moderated by Collider's Maggie Lovitt , where they were asked about the future of Sandfall, whether it involves a DLC expansion for their masterpiece, a new title in the Clair Obscur world, or something else. The team hasn't been entirely quiet since Expedition 33 arrived, releasing a "Thank You" update with new content including Verso's Drafts in celebration of their Game of the Year win, but there's been no word about anything major. Starr wanted to remind everyone that this is still a small team and games of that magnitude take time .

"Obviously we're not supposed to speak for Sandfall Interactive, but they're a small team. I think that update was a beautiful one. I hope you've enjoyed and enjoyed taking pictures. We've enjoyed seeing everyone's pictures from that update. I can't say what they're working on. I imagine they're working on their next project; good for them, I hope so. No pressure! But yeah, they're an amazing team, and every now and again Guillaume sends us little updates. Not from the game he's making, just like proof of life."

Your answers have pointed to one Oscar Best Picture winner above all others. This is the film that was made for the way your mind works.

You are drawn to films that operate on multiple levels simultaneously — that begin in one genre and quietly, brilliantly migrate into another. Bong Joon-ho's Parasite is a film about class, desire, and the architecture of inequality that manages to be darkly funny, deeply suspenseful, and genuinely shocking across a single extraordinary running time. Your instinct is for cinema that hides its true intentions until the moment it's ready to reveal them. Parasite is exactly that — a film that rewards close attention and punishes assumptions, right up to its devastating final image.

You want it all — and this film gives you all of it. The Daniels' Everything Everywhere All at Once is one of the most maximalist films ever made: action comedy, multiverse sci-fi, family drama, existential crisis, and a genuinely earned emotional core that sneaks up on you amid the chaos. You are someone who responds to ambition, who doesn't want cinema to choose between being entertaining and being meaningful. This film refuses that choice entirely. It is overwhelming by design, and its overwhelming nature is precisely the point — because the feeling of being crushed by infinite possibility is exactly what it's about.

You are drawn to cinema on a grand scale — films that understand history not as a backdrop but as a force, and that place their characters inside that force and watch what happens. Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer is a film about the terrifying gap between what we can do and what we should do, told with the full weight of one of the most consequential moments in human history behind it. You want your films to feel important without feeling self-important — to earn their ambition through sheer craft and the gravity of their subject. Oppenheimer does exactly that. It is enormous, complicated, and refuses easy comfort.

You are drawn to films that foreground their own construction — that make the how of the filmmaking part of the what it's about. Alejandro González Iñárritu's Birdman, shot to appear as a single continuous take, is cinema examining itself through the cracked mirror of a fading actor's ego. You respond to formal daring, to the feeling that a film is doing something that probably shouldn't be possible. Michael Keaton's performance and Emmanuel Lubezki's restless camera create something genuinely unlike anything else — a film that is simultaneously about creativity, relevance, self-destruction, and the impossibility of ever truly knowing if your work means anything at all.

You are drawn to cinema that trusts silence, that refuses to explain itself, and that treats dread as a form of meaning. The Coen Brothers' No Country for Old Men is a film about the arrival of a new kind of evil — implacable, arbitrary, and utterly indifferent to the moral frameworks we use to make sense of the world. It is one of the most formally controlled films ever made, and its controlled restraint is what makes it so terrifying. You want your films to haunt you, not comfort you. You are not interested in resolution if resolution would be dishonest. No Country for Old Men is honest in a way that most cinema never dares to be.

Video games, even compared to other mediums, are remarkably complex creatures that combine so many talented individuals of varying skillsets. The biggest productions typically take five, or often more, years to make with much larger teams than what Sandfall is working with. It makes for a sometimes awkward period afterward of just talking about a game to publications, expos, and more while the next project comes together in the background. "It's a weird thing making video games," Starr added. "You make it, and then you have to spend a year and a half just kind of talking about it, and I think a lot of people are just creatives. I don't mind working on stuff. I do love talking about it ; that's when you really get into the meat of the creative part."

There has been plenty said about Expedition 33 since its release, and much more conversation to come as gamers continue to reflect on the characters and themes behind one of the best titles of the 2020s so far. Starr feels confident that the team is the type to be itching to make something new and unique, even if it takes a minute. "I think they're creative people, so whatever they work on next, I know it's going to be amazing. Let them cook. There's a reason why this game is so special." In the meantime, Starr has added a few more notable titles to his resume, joining Destiny developers Bungie on their new extraction shooter, Marathon , and lending his voice to the tactical RPG Ledgerbound .

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. Stay tuned here at Collider for more on what comes next for Sandfall after their monumental success.

items.title: Blue Dragon And 8 Other Completely Unhinged RPG Battle Themes You Need To Listen To
items.summary: I have been informed of the battle theme to Blue Dragon and I have several questions
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Earthbound Music RPG

Earlier today, my partner came into the room and asked if I’d ever be interested in playing the 2007 Xbox 360 RPG Blue Dragon . This was sort of a weird question, even in our very gaming-centric household, but apparently the reason he asked is that the game is getting an unofficial PC port (as spotted by VGC ).

That’s cool! It’s great that it won’t be stuck on the Xbox 360 anymore and will be accessible to more people. I politely declined to play Blue Dragon at this time (I am busy), but later today the game must have still been on his mind, because my partner sent me this:

That is, I kid you not, apparently the regular-ass battle music in Blue Dragon , a game composed by…Nobuo Uematsu? The Final Fantasy guy?!

Oh my God. This is great. You get like three measures of whatever guitar and then this guy just starts wailing out of tune. And it has lyrics that invoke a ridiculous anime OP from the 90s or something. All while rocking out as hard as possible so that you never lose the momentum of battle. Hell yeah!

I love RPGs, and I love an RPG that’s not afraid to do stuff with its music that’s unconventional. A boss theme that’s calm and soothing rather than intense, a field theme that’s unexpectedly sad, lyrics, rare or specialized instruments, I love it all.

It’s Friday, so in the spirit of Blue Dragon , let’s celebrate its arrival on PC by listening to some other totally unhinged, wacky, or out there regular RPG battle themes together. I will try to stick to regular battle themes, ones for normal ol’ enemies, because if I busted out the boss battles, we’d be here all day.

Let’s start with an oldie but goodie: Pepper Steak (or, if you run with the typo, Peper Steak). Oh, sorry, you think this one is disturbing? Yeah, it’s meant to be. OFF is an RPG about a baseball player “purifying” a messed-up world of blood and meat and plastic by murdering all the ghosts who live in it. Yes, really. Pepper Steak is probably its most infamous theme, with its weird, haunting swing and frequent dissonance and irregular rhythms. Alias Conrad Coldwood, the composer, was unable to return for the 2025 remake, so Toby Fox and Camelia stepped in to make themes for each different zone instead of one overarching Pepper Steak replacement. I have not a single bad word to say about anything Fox has ever composed, but I do think (and he seemed to agree in his statement about it) that it was always going to be impossible to replace Pepper Steak.

I haven’t personally played Shadow Hearts , but I guess this battle theme plays when you go to Japan? Anyway, someone has tried to explain the plot of this game to me a few times, and it hasn’t stuck, but dang if this isn’t an absolutely bonkers thing to have as your regular, normal battle theme for regular, normal enemies for a good chunk of the game.

Nintendo, when are you putting this on the Nintendo music app? This is just workout music. Which I guess is, like, appropriate for the game. But you didn’t have to go this hard.

I don’t need to explain why this is in here, right? This is just Johnny B. Goode by Chuck Berry . The Mother games are all music licensing hell, and I strongly suspect that similar issues in Mother 3 are why we’ll never get an official Western localization. I cannot believe they just put this classic into Earthbound and attached it to the hippie battles. Wild choice.

I strongly felt that something from The World Ends With You belonged on this list due to the series’ daring commitment, on the Nintendo DS of all things, to make its entire soundtrack a straight-up rock and pop album. I was having trouble deciding which theme to go with, though, because while they’re all good, none of them really strike me as the level of off-the-charts wild that the Blue Dragon theme does.

Then I remembered that Transformation, Minamimoto’s absolutely fantastic boss theme, enters the regular battle song rotation in Week 3. Let’s GO. (The remix in NEO is pretty great, too!)

I want to take us briefly in another direction with this list, away from the hard, intense rock songs, and ask you all: what business does this have being a battle theme? This is a song for a minigame in Mario Party , or some pleasant phone hold music. I always find myself bouncing up and down a little while it’s playing. This is another one with a pretty great remix version in the remake. If you want a bonus second theme along these same lines of upbeat minigame music, enjoy Kiss of Jealousy from Live A Live , and from the remake of that too!

items.title: 1 year later, the best Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 quote still lives rent-free in my head
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Rebecca Corgan Published Aug 7, 2026, 1:30 PM EDT FYI ‘Wheee’ balances ‘whooo’ is still so true

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Getting through an average day in 2026 requires resilience – the basic ability to weather mundane-but-constant highs, like a good news text from a friend, and lows, like realizing you need to head to the store (again) to pick up an item you forgot (again). Achieving that ability to manage everything going on at once is hard. It’s tempting to allow yourself to ricochet from high to low in rollercoaster fashion – but we need to give our brains a break. We must…achieve…balance.

Easier said than done, of course. So let’s work to avoid burnout, take a deep breath in and out, and remember the immortal words of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s Esquie: “I too am ‘Whooo.’ But I’m also ‘Wheee!’ So the ‘Wheee’ balances the ‘Whooo.’”

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive via Polygon Esquie’s mantra, here, comes from one of the many camp conversations you can enjoy during downtime in an otherwise tumultuous game about grief . In this quiet aside, Esquie (an enormous, floating, and endearingly oblivious companion who’s arguably the emotional center of the whole game) is speaking to his dear friend Verso, one of the game’s traumatized playable leads. They are discussing their mutual friend François, who has gone quiet since losing his own closest friend. Verso mentions that François used to be all ‘wheee,’ but these days he’s a bit more ‘whooo.’ These are Esquie’s shorthand terms, we learn, for happy and sad. Already, this shows-not-tells us exactly how close these two are (we’ve all got baffling inside jokes turned vocab with our nearest and dearest) and allows us to feel immediately what it’s like inside their relationship. This is one of the realest-feeling moments in the game for me, despite everything going on in Expedition 33.

But Verso’s not done talking. He asks Esquie which of the two – ‘wheee’ or ‘whooo’ – is more Esquie’s vibe these days. Esquie does not pick. He’s whooo, sure, I mean, look at the world these characters are living through . But he is also wheee; he gets to tackle existential problems by spending time with his best friend, which is a lovely win. And this feels very realistic. Even when things are darkest, there’s usually something happening that we can hold onto, a little light to keep us feeling human and remind us that we’ll be okay.

It’s not surprising that such a simple yet resonant line came from a real-life emotionally nuanced moment. The game’s lead writer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, told Polygon back in May 2025 that this particular scene came together in the middle of the night , when she was too tired to do anything other than articulate the way the moment should sound. We’ve all been there, right? Life happens, and words fail us. We just sit back in our chairs and sigh. And communicate those feelings as best we can. And it feels so relieving, bonding, and right when the people around us just get what we’re trying to say, even when words fail.

So! Whatever the universe has in store for you today, remember you are both ‘whooo’ and ‘wheee.’ Perhaps you’re bracing for bad news that hasn’t landed yet, and you are ‘whooo;’ perhaps your pet will curl close to you on the couch later, and you shall be ‘wheee.’ Breathe deep through whichever happens first, allow yourself Esquie’s gift of perspective, and remember – You and me and Esquie: We’ve got this.

items.title: "It's a sad decision." Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks
items.summary: Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.
items.content:
Home Interviews “It’s a sad decision.” Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.

Interviews 2026-07-29 00:01 Genki 4 Epic Games Japan and Sandfall Interactive recently hosted a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem event in Yokohama, Japan, where the developers shared technical insights into the making of 2025’s Game of the Year. Following the event, AUTOMATON sat down with the team and took the opportunity to ask about their thoughts on physical game releases. With PlayStation set to end game disc production in 2028, the developers briefly reflected on why they insisted on releasing Expedition 33 physically despite the added challenges, and discussed why they believe physical editions remain important to video games as a medium.

Guillaume Broche – Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Tom Guillermin – Sandfall Interactive Co-founder and CTO Alan Reynaud – Lead Character and Concept Artist Alexandre Breton – Technical Artist

For more about Sandfall Interactive’s Japanese influences, thoughts on Unreal Engine, and studio upsizing, check out part one of this interview .

— PlayStation recently announced that it will end physical disk production in 2028. What are your thoughts on that?

Guillaume Broche: Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores. And even if nowadays, I play mainly on PC myself, we have a lot of people on the team who play on PS5 and love to collect physical discs. I think it’s part of the beauty of art too – that it’s something tangible that you can touch. I completely appreciate that people want to have their rows of DVDs and games and just feel that they own them. So I think it’s a shame. I mean, business-wise, I can understand why it may make sense, but I think in terms of the artistry of video games, it’s a sad decision.

Tom Guillermin: In our discussions with our publisher prior to the release of Expedition 33, the question of whether or not to do a physical release cropped up. A physical release adds more constraints because you have to account for the production time of the physical items, and you also earn less money per copy.

But for us, physical was something special. We also felt that the game could be special to players, and that they would want to, as Guillaume said, hold it in their hands.

So even though it made things harder and meant less money per unit, it was important for us to provide players who want to have the physical game in their hands with an option. Because that’s what we value as players too.

Guillaume Broche: To add to that, there were two very strong moments when the game released. After launch, we went to a video game store to buy our own game (laughs). Just as a gesture. And another strong memory I have is when someone from Japan sent me a picture [of our game] from a video game store – in Akihabara I think – in Japanese writing and all. I felt like a kid when I saw it. I was like “Yeah, it’s real!” It starts feeling real when you see it in stores. Alan Reynaud: Even now when I’m going to the supermarket or something, if I see our game in a store, it always makes my day. It’s a bit selfish, because it’s our game, but it always makes me go “Oh!”

Knowing that may not be possible again makes me a bit sad. And maybe it’s the child in me, but I like to go outside, buy a game, and come back home with it. It’s a nice feeling.

Alexandre Breton: And it’s not just because it’s “our game.” I think what’s cool [about physical games in general] is that a few years later, you’ll have your box, and you can hold it and look at the title and remember all the memories that are linked to the game.

Alan Reynaud: I think the same principle can apply to manga. It’s nice to read on your phone and stuff, but having a real book is just a different feeling. And I don’t think we could imagine a world where manga is just scanned and stored on your computer. It would be sad to not have it in your library. I think the same applies for games. Sure, it makes more sense business-wise, but you lose the spirit of it.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available for PC ( Steam ), PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Unreal Engine 5 Made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Possible, Yet It Makes A Nintendo Switch 2 Port A Big Challenge
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive reveals how Unreal Engine 5 made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 possible, but also how it makes a Switch 2 port challenging
items.content:
Since its launch in 2022, Unreal Engine 5 has been one of the most controversial game engines from Epic Games , mostly due to how demanding it is on PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and PC , as well as the performance issues it brings. Although the engine has been significantly improved since , public perception hasn't changed much, with many gamers considering it one of the worst things to happen to modern gaming. However, many developers don't share this sentiment, as Sandfall Interactive , the studio behind the 2025 Game of the Year Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , couldn't have made the game without it.

"For starters, Unreal Engine has all the tools you need to make a game that looks big, even if you’re not a big team," Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Guillaume Broche said to Automaton . "And we were very lucky with the release timing of some of Unreal’s newer tools. Unreal Engine 5 itself came at the right time in production, then MetaHuman came at the right time, and so did Nanite and Lumen – everything came at the right time. So we were very lucky with that."

The best thing about Unreal Engine 5 is that it gives developers all the tools they need to make something great, Broche continued, while heaping praise on Blueprints , the visual scripting system that will eventually be deprecated in Unreal Engine 6 , once the new Verse/Scene Graph framework matures. "Blueprints, especially, are very important. Blueprints are like a visual scripting method that allows pretty much anybody in the team to write code thanks to how easy it is. It’s like chaining blocks together. In our studio, we have four programmers, but every game designer and every technical artist uses Blueprints to make game logic or environment logic, and that’s crucial for us to be able to ship this kind of game and this kind of quality."

Technical Artist Alexandre Breton also had only praise for Unreal Engine 5's Blueprints . "Blueprints are part of an ecosystem. It’s visual scripting, so it’s very ludic and you can learn it very easily. It’s part of an ecosystem because a lot of people are using it and sharing content, so you can also find resources like tutorials everywhere. You can also find Blueprint Packs and learn from them. People give them away for free or sell them, and it’s never too expensive. Overall, it’s a system that’s very cool to use."

Although several games powered by Unreal Engine 5 have made their way onto the Nintendo Switch 2 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has yet to do so. The team is interested in a port, but there are technical challenges that are even more daunting for a small studio like Sandfall Interactive .

"It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio," said studio Co-founder and CTO Tom Guillermin .

While some Unreal Engine 5 features don't work on Nintendo Switch 2 , which we have known for a while, Lumen Lite could make the port slightly less challenging. "They’re introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do," said Lead Character and Concept Artist Alan Reynaud .

Considering the high quality of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , it would be a shame if Nintendo Switch 2 owners would never get to experience it. At the same time, it's understandable how Sandfall Interactive sees the port as a challenge, given the studio's small size. The current generation Nintendo system has already seen some impressive ports like Cyberpunk 2077 and the Final Fantasy VII Remake series, but they were handled by much bigger studios with developers and resources to invest.

Hopefully Lumen Lite , which has been created specifically for handhelds like the Nintendo Switch 2 , will help this port become a reality.

About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. After joining Wccftech gaming section in 2015, he quickly expanded his video gaming coverage with in-depth reporting, interviews with iconic industry figures such as Grasshopper Manufacture founder and No More Heroes creator Goichi "Suda51" Suda, Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami, Team NINJA's president and Nioh series director Fumihiko Yasuda, and Silent Hill creator Keiichiro Toyama, reviews and on-the-ground coverage of major industry events such as Gamescom and E3. items.title: Expedition 33 Dev Teases "Drastic Decisions" for Next Game
items.summary: Sandfall has some interesting words to say when it comes to their next game following Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.
items.content:
One of the biggest success stories this generation is undoubtedly RPG hit, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the debut game from Sandfall Interactive.

While the studio has already confirmed that we’ll see more games in the franchise , it seems that what the developer has planned isn’t just a straight-up sequel.

On the contrary, based on what was recently said by the studio’s boss, we might be in for something different than what we’re expecting.

In a video interview , Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Guillaume Broche, mentioned they didn’t develop the RPG to please anyone, and added that some people might not like their next game, given they’re making some “drastic decisions.”

Not only that, but the developer also commented on the pressures of wanting to expand the studio, high expectations and more.

Broche mentioned (via YouTube translate), “We spent five years where, I think, overall, the dev team was just so happy to be working together. It went really well. And doing that again in our little den in Montpellier—that’s what we love. And that’s what people love, too, so why change?”

He added, “I think there’s a bit of that pressure we can put on ourselves if, psychologically, we start veering off in one direction or another—telling ourselves: we’re going to go bigger, we’re going to expand the studio because expectations are higher, so we’ll just keep growing.”

Broche also mentioned how they’re going to stick to making games that they love, and not really concerned whether their follow-up project isn’t as popular.

“And then we end up with games that, personally, I don’t play because I don’t like them. So we’re going to stick to making games that we love. If people like them, great,” Broche said, and added, “If it doesn’t, oh well. Do you already know that the next game won’t be as popular? I have no idea. I don’t really care.”

“It’s weird to say, but we didn’t make the first game to please anyone. And I think that’s why it worked. So for the next game, we’ll make some drastic decisions too, and maybe people won’t like it. That’s life. Whether people follow us or not is their decision,” Broche answered.

All in all, Broche doesn’t want the studio to be crushed under the pressure of gamers for their next project, but also admitted that if it sells zero copies (low sales), that they’ll have problems.

While Sandfall hasn’t announced what their next game is, most people — including me — assume it’ll be a follow-up to Expedition 33. We haven’t heard anything about it, but I think I can confidently predict that it won’t sell “zero” copies.

Whatever Sandfall’s next project is, you can bet a lot of people will be keeping a close eye on it, and that includes us.

Speaking of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the developers recently released a new game update that added more devs in the credits and more.

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Charlie Cox has finally played Clair Obscur: Expedition 33—a bit
items.summary: The star of Stardust and Daredevil previously admitted to not having tried the game he stars in.
items.content:
The star of Stardust and Daredevil previously admitted to not having tried the game he stars in.

(Image credit: Kepler) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter I don't expect every actor to play the videogames they're connected to, and have a lot of respect for the way Walton Goggins just straight-up said he hasn't played Fallout and won't play Fallout . Good for him. You don't want to join us down here in the pit, spending the rest of our lives trying to convince people Fallout 2 wasn't as good as the first one. Get out while you still can.

When Charlie Cox admitted he hadn't played Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , even though he voices Gustave in it, that seemed fair enough to me. It's a 45-hour JRPG with a frankly quite divisive ending. You don't need that in your life while also trying to maintain Daredevil's abs.

In a more recent interview with our comrades at GamesRadar , however, Cox said he finally got around to playing it. A bit. "Not the whole thing," he added. "I haven't completed it." He's seen the impressive introductory area, though. "I've played the opening bit for a while and kind of walked around and met the people and garnered the information and all that kind of stuff. Not very well."

Cox highlighted how different Clair Obscur felt when compared to the videogames he grew up with, like Goldeneye, Mario Kart, and FIFA 98. "They weren't, like, stories that were so carefully carved out and created over the course of a game with the level of detail and the way in which information is received. It's not just all spelled out—you discover these things as you go on through the game," Cox said.

It must be an uncanny experience, playing a videogame as a character you've provided the voice for. "It didn't really feel like me... I didn't really think of it as me, I thought of it as Gustave."

J.K. Simmons hasn't played Baldur's Gate 3 or any of his games, but he loves Portal 2: 'I could have done the feature film, or the play, or whatever' Ray Chase, the voice of Cyclops in X-Men '97, has '1,000 freaking hours' in Slay the Spire and is running a 'smell build' in Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2: ' I wear perfumes and walk into battle with my fancy boy outfit' Clair Obscur is flawed on purpose, says director: 'Games that try to be perfect, that try to fix all their flaws—they're usually just really boring' Though he didn't say whether he'll go back to play more, I suspect Cox won't be collecting all the achievements any time soon. He seemed sensibly incredulous when he said, "there are people who've played it, there are people who've completed it, there are people who have 100%ed it, which—as far as I could work out—is 50-plus hours, maybe 100 hours, sometimes, of gameplay." Honestly, that is too much, and he's right to say it.

items.title: The developers of Clair Obscur gave me an interview and some advice
items.summary: We spoke about the game's finale (don't worry, there are spoiler warnings), the best Pictos, and what I can be doing better.
items.content:
Stephen Totilo Mar 27, 2026 35 3 1 Share Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Screenshot: Sandfall Interactive, captured by Game File This story, perhaps appropriately, goes on a bit longer than you might expect, past what may feel like the conclusion.

This was not by design. In my business of reporting, you can’t plan surprise endings. But it is what delightfully happened.

This story is merely an accurate account of my absurd endeavor from earlier this month, when I tried to finally play through 2025’s most acclaimed video game, the role-playing phenomenon Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , in a sudden rush.

I had a deadline: a date when I expected to have a chance to chat about Clair Obscur with some of its creators. We would perhaps discuss the game’s ending, which, in their business of making video games, they could plan for.

I will get to all of that. I will get to Thursday night, March 12, when I spoke to two of Clair Obscur’s creators, discussed the ending and got myself an in-person consultation about my characters’ builds.

It’s Sunday, March 8 and I have downloaded Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to the portable ROG Xbox Ally X , a Switch-looking device that can run games offered via Xbox Game Pass. At this point, I have only played a little past the prologue of Clair Obscur, back on an Xbox in my house. Cloud saving has transferred my progress to the portable. In the game, our protagonist Gustave and his sort-of sister Maelle have set out on Expedition 33, the latest annual beach landing of adventurers who hope they will be the ones to take down the distant and mysterious paintress, who somehow, magically annihilates everyone of a certain age each year.

I know I’ve given myself barely enough time to play through this game ahead of Thursday, when Clair Obscur is likely to win another pile of awards at the former Game Developers Conference (now GDC Festival of Gaming) and when I’ll be backstage with an opportunity to interview the winners.

In the weeks prior, I’ve been busy writing and reporting and, in terms of actually using a controller, playing through Resident Evils .

Just back in February, I had been backstage at a different gaming awards event, where I’d met some of the makers of Clair Obscur and where I’d not spoken to them about the game, because I had other coverage goals for my chats with the winners.

For the Game Developers Choice Awards on March 12, though, I want to talk about the games. My friend urges me on. You should try to finish Clair Obscur, he says. They haven’t spoken about the ending all that much, yet it’s all the game’s fans talk about. You gotta find out what happens, he says, even if you just have to watch a video. Perish the thought.

So I’m on United Airlines flight 1777 from EWR to SFO, comfortably seated in window seat 39A. My Ally X is in my hands, and Clair Obscur is running, well before takeoff. I’ve boarded fairly early. Soon, a man with long curly hair takes the middle seat next to me. There is still plenty of elbow room for me, and I start playing. Best I can tell, the man in the middle seat soon starts a nap.

Gustave, alongside a magically powered woman named Lune, are fighting enemies called Nevrons in dramatic turn-based fights. They reunite with red-haired Maelle. As the plane takes off and begins to cross the United States, things are going well. I’m loving the combat and the look of the game’s world.

Before my plane lands, I reach the end of Clair Obscur’s first act. Big twist! I’ve been rushing, avoiding sidequests, and, wow. I did not see that coming. I’m stunned, but I don’t think anyone on the flight notices. I make sure not to disturb the curly-haired guy next to me, who I think at this point is watching a movie?

After my flight lands, I text my friend to confirm that I have not seen Clair Obscur’s wildest turn. I have not.

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
